51567580.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to His-tagged human p47phox (151 to 386 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3) pLysS assessed as dissociation constant at steady state by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR). SPR measurements were performed on a Pioneer F5 SPR instrument (Sartorius, Göttingen, Germany) and data were analyzed using the Qdat Data Analysis Tool version 4.3.2. All experiments were performed at 25 °C. Pioneer HisCap Biosensor chips (Sartorius) were installed and preconditioned with successive injections of 10 mM HCl (2 × 16 μL), 50 mM NaOH (2 × 100 μL), 0.1% v/v SDS (2 × 16 μL), and 300 mM EDTA (pH 8) (2 × 100 μL) to the analyte and reference channel. The protein, His-tagged p47phoxSH3A–B, was immobilized to the analyte channel by histidine capture via a nickel (Ni2+) chelation step and a subsequent amine coupling procedure using HBS (10 mM Heps, 150 mM NaCl, 0.005% tween, pH 7.4) as immobilization buffer. Injections for the immobilization process were as follows: 350 mM EDTA (1 × 20 μL), 500 μM NiSO4 (1 × 40 μL; only to analyte channel), NHS/EDC mix (1 × 30 μL; 50 mM N-hydroxysuccinimide and 200 mM 1-ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide), p47phoxSH3A–B (1 × 130 μL; only to analyte channel), 3.5 μM or 7 μM in running buffer, for low and high immobilization levels, respectively), 1 M ethanolamine (1 × 35 μL), and 350 mM EDTA (1 × 20 μL). Compound experiments were performed with HBS supplemented with 4% v/v DMSO as running buffer. Microcalibration (low limit 3% and high limit 5%) was performed to adjust for DMSO bulk effects. All sensorgrams were corrected for buffer bulk effects and unspecific binding of the samples to the chip matrix by sample blank (running buffer injections) and reference channel subtraction. Compounds were injected in 2-fold dilution series at 30 μL/min flow rate following 30 s of dissociation. The p22phox149–168 peptide was used as a positive control for assessing the activity of the sensor surface during the experiment (30 μL/min flow rate; 180 s of dissociation). For the steady state analysis, response units at equilibrium for each concentration of an analyte were plotted against the injected compound concentrations and curve fitted to a Langmuir (1:1) binding isotherm model to determine the dissociation constant (Kd). In addition, a kinetic one-site association and dissociation fitting was applied, calculating the dissociation constant Kd as the relation of the kinetic parameters of the dissociation and association events, koff and kon, respectively. Immobilization levels (Rimmob) were detected after the final EDTA injection as a part of the immobilization process in response units with 1 RU ≈ 1 pg/mm2. The theoretical maximum response at saturation (Rmax) for 100% protein activity was calculated as Rmax = (MW-analyte/MW-ligand) × Rimmob with MW-ligand and MW-analyte being molecular weights of His-tagged p47phoxSH3A–B (17300 Da) and test compounds, respectively. The ratio between the experimentally determined Rmax at steady-state and the theoretical Rmax values provides an estimation of the percentage of active immobilized protein. The activity levels of bivalent compounds (10 and 33) were compared with that of the peptide control p22phox149–168 (known to bind 1:1 to p47phoxSH3A–B) to evaluate the stoichiometric ratio of bivalent compounds binding to p47phoxSH3A–B.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Characterization of the direct binding to p47phoxSH3A–B by SPR and ITC. (A) Representative SPR sensorgrams (left) of compound 10 and 33 injected in 2-fold serial dilutions over immobilized p47phoxSH3A–B, and plots of equilibrium binding responses (right) at the end of the analyte injections against the tested concentrations. Sensorgrams are blank injection and reference surface subtracted. The sensorgrams were globally fitted to a 1:1 kinetic interaction model (red lines) to determine the kon and koff rate constants and thereby calculate the “kinetic” Kd values (Table 9). The equilibrium binding responses were also fitted to a one-site binding model to determine the steady-state Kd values (Table 9). (B) Representative ITC thermograms showing binding of compound 10 and 33 to p47phoxSH3A–B. The compounds (250 μM) were titrated into p47phoxSH3A–B (25 μM) in 19 × 2 μL or 24 × 1.5 μL injections. The red line indicates fitting to a one-site binding model.
